problem:
A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=4\sqrt{t},$ where $t>0$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=\frac{7}{3}\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=1\,\text{s},$ determine the moment in time when the particle is stationary.

The particle is stationary at $t=$
{{field-1}}$\text{s}.$
worked_solution:
The particle is stationary when $v=0\,\text{m}/\text{s}.$

First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (4\sqrt{t})\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{8}{3}{t}^{3/2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C,$ we use the fact that $v(1)=\frac{7}{3}.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{7}{3} & =\frac{8}{3}(1)^{3/2}+C \\ \frac{7}{3} & =\frac{8}{3}+C \\ C & =-\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=\frac{8}{3}{t}^{3/2}-\frac{1}{3}.$

Now, we find the moments in time when $v=0\,\text{m}/\text{s}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{8}{3}{t}^{3/2}-\frac{1}{3} & =0 \\ \frac{8}{3}{t}^{3/2} & =\frac{1}{3} \\ 8{t}^{3/2} & =1 \\ {t}^{3/2} & =\frac{1}{8} \\ t & ={(\frac{1}{8})}^{2/3}=\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the particle is stationary when $t=\frac{1}{4}\,\text{s}.$
